The effect of biofouling-induced drag forces on the performance of a point absorber WEC was studied. Because these drag forces are nonlinear, the dynamics of the WEC were simulated using the tool WEC-Sim. In general, biofouling was found to reduce the WEC’s optimal damping point, power, peak displacement, and peak velocity. For the operating point of H = 2 m and at the WEC’s resonant period (12 s), the average PTO power was found to decrease by 15% after growing a 10−1 m layer of hard biofouling. It was shown that decreasing the PTO damping by 20% recovers some of theinevitablepowerlossduetobiofoulingbutislimited to only a small percentage of that power loss. At this sameoperatingpoint,thepeakvelocityandpeakposition werefoundtodecreasebyapproximately10%,withthat decrease being greater at larger wave periods.
